title: Length difference for the ideal of denominators over a one dimensional Noetherian local ring without embedded primes
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For a one dimensional Noetherian local ring A without embedded primes, a finite module M with no embedded associated primes and full support, nonzerodivisors a and b, and I the ideal of x with x(a/b) in A, the lemma asserts (a/b)IM subset M and expresses the length difference length_A(M/(a/b)IM) - length_A(M/IM) as the sum over the minimal primes of length_{A_{q_i}}(M_{q_i}) ord_{A/q_i}(a/b) (statement lines 18593-18618). The proof first turns the hypotheses into a statement about associated primes: no embedded primes for M together with full support forces Ass(M) to be exactly the set of minimal primes, so a and b are nonzerodivisors on M (proof lines 18621-18624). Then it computes the left hand side by a four-term chain of length identities, using that the injective maps b : M -> bM and a : M -> aM carry (a/b)IM to aIM and IM to aIM respectively, which reduces it to length_A(M/aM) - length_A(M/bM) (proof lines 18625-18640). The final identification with the two order functions is the cited additivity formula (proof lines 18641-18645). The manipulation of the length difference through the two injective rescalings is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
